title: CedarDB wants one database to handle both transactions and analytics, as AI agents raise the stakes
key_facts: CedarDB is a Munich-based database engine spun out of the Technical University of Munich, built on the research project Umbra.
It supports both analytical queries and operational (transaction) workloads in one system, which CEO and co-founder Moritz Sichert says matters more with agentic AI.
It is compatible with PostgreSQL, which keeps switching costs low and matches what LLMs know best.
On Wednesday (14 Oct 2026) it announced limited availability of CedarDB Cloud on stage at TechCrunch Disrupt, where it is one of 21 startups in the Startup Battlefield.
CedarDB Enterprise (on-premise) and a free Community Edition were announced in May of last year with a EUR 5.3 million (about $6 million) seed round.
The company has 14 people and Sichert expects to raise its next round once the cloud offering gets traction.
Databricks launched a similar unified architecture, LTAP, at its June Data + AI Summit.
quote_evidence: Databases have traditionally been built for one of two jobs.

It is too early to tell how disruptive this might be
why_it_matters_hint: A small startup is bringing a combined database to the cloud just as bigger rivals chase the same idea for AI agents.
notes: Interview-based; claims of speed are the company's.
